title: HUD Five-Year Minimum for Remaining Tenure Payments on a Move to the HECM Line of Credit
content:
For the payment release of a Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) loan moving off scheduled payments onto the HECM Line of Credit, Cedarline applies the HUD five-year minimum to the remaining payments:

- on a tenure-based plan where twelve times the difference between the plan's tenure age horizon (100 years on the HECM Tenure Payment Plan and the HECM Modified Tenure Plan) and the borrower's age is less than 60, the remaining payments are 60;
- on any other tenure-based plan they are twelve times that difference;
- on a term-based plan they are the scheduled payment term in months less the scheduled payments already disbursed on the loan.

The borrower's age is the youngest borrower's age at closing plus the whole years from the closing date to the handling date.

| Borrower's age (tenure plan, horizon 100) | Twelve times the difference | Remaining payments |
|---|---|---|
| 94 | 72 | 72 |
| 95 | 60 | 60 (not less than 60) |
| 96 | 48 | 60 |
| 101 | minus 12 | 60 |

*Term-based case (hypothetical):* a 120-month term with 115 payments disbursed leaves 5 remaining payments; the minimum does not apply to a term-based plan.
